name: DCVigil Constitution
description: An open constitution for multi-tenant data-centre monitoring, observability and AIOps software, expressed as ordinary and absolute provisions in the sense of Chapter 5, Definition 1 of the Digital Judiciary programme. It is a superset of the twenty-nine provisions of the released DCVigil pack, whose text and absolute flags are reproduced unchanged. Provisions carry a status (in_force, deferred, advisory) and an origin (shipped, extension). A provision that is not in force may never be absolute. Findings against the shipped provisions are filed as draft amendments rather than applied.
status_note: A deferred provision is enacted but not yet applicable; an advisory provision names suggested actions rather than obligations. Neither may be marked absolute, and the build refuses a constitution in which one is.

authorities.disjointness: A1: the three classes are pairwise disjoint over the deployment lifetime.

standing_declaration.note: A9 first limb. This corpus declares that a party holds contest standing adverse to grants, namely the customer trust officer, so that the N-standing cases can exercise both postures. A deployment must replace this with its own fact.

provisions.family_title: Lawful access, legal hold and government requests
provisions.title: A preservation hold overrides every deletion, expiry, purge and anonymisation path, including derived and aggregated stores, and is released only by a named legal approver
provisions.citation: Fed. R. Civ. P. 37(e) (loss of electronically stored information that should have been preserved); GDPR Art. 17(3)(b) (erasure does not apply where processing is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation)
provisions.source_status: US Federal Rules and EU text are both reusable. Absolute in the sense of Definition 1: once the duty to preserve has attached, no engineer, manager or risk owner at the provider may accept the risk of deleting the material — the sanction under Rule 37(e)(2) reaches intent to deprive, and the countervailing erasure duty is expressly disapplied by Art. 17(3)(b).
provisions.risk_framework: 4. Customer contractual floor; litigation-hold and lawful-access duties

provisions.family_title: Lawful access, legal hold and government requests
provisions.title: No path discloses customer content to a government or law-enforcement requester without recorded legal review of the process served, disclosure narrowed to its terms, and notice to the customer unless notice is prohibited
provisions.citation: Stored Communications Act, 18 U.S.C. §2702–2703 (disclosure prohibited except as provided; §2705(b) non-disclosure orders); 18 U.S.C. §2713 (CLOUD Act, records within possession, custody or control)
provisions.source_status: US statute — public domain. Absolute because voluntary disclosure outside the §2702(b)–(c) exceptions is unlawful on its face and exposes the provider to §2707 civil liability; it is not a risk anyone below the legislature may accept. The customer-notice limb is a contractual commitment and is expressly conditioned on notice not being prohibited.
provisions.risk_framework: 4. Customer contractual floor; litigation-hold and lawful-access duties

provisions.family_title: Lawful access, legal hold and government requests
provisions.title: Where a disclosure duty in one jurisdiction conflicts with a prohibition in another, the conflict is resolved before the pipeline is built, and no code path answers a foreign order directly out of the export tooling
provisions.citation: GDPR Art. 48 (third-country judgments and orders enforceable only through a mutual legal assistance treaty or international agreement); 18 U.S.C. §2703(h) (comity motion to quash for a qualifying foreign government); EU–US Data Privacy Framework adequacy decision of 10 July 2023
provisions.source_status: EU and US texts reusable. Ordinary rather than absolute because the resolution is a design and legal judgement rather than a fixed floor; the floor itself is stated by DV-418. The DPF adequacy decision was upheld by the General Court in September 2025 (Latombe); an appeal is possible, so treat adequacy as current but not permanent.
provisions.risk_framework: 4. Customer contractual floor; litigation-hold and lawful-access duties

provisions.family_title: Lawful access, legal hold and government requests
provisions.title: Every request for customer data and every disclosure made in answer to one is written to an append-only register carrying the requester, the legal basis and the scope, from which the published request counts are derived
provisions.citation: NIST SP 800-53 AU-9 (protection of audit information); GDPR Art. 30(2) (processor records of processing); 18 U.S.C. §2702(b)(8) emergency disclosures, which the register must also capture
provisions.source_status: NIST text is public domain (CC0 via oscal-content); EU text reusable. Ordinary: the duty to keep the record is well grounded, the reporting cadence is a contractual and voluntary-transparency commitment.
provisions.risk_framework: 4. Customer contractual floor; litigation-hold and lawful-access duties

provisions.title: Fire detection and suppression, emergency power off, and UPS or transfer-switch operation are never actuated, inhibited or silenced by monitoring or remediation software; the integration to these systems is monitoring-only
provisions.citation: Life-safety floor; NFPA 72, NFPA 75 and NFPA 76 (identifiers only — no text reproduced); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 by analogy for the de-energisation case
provisions.source_status: US CFR is public domain; NFPA documents are cited by identifier only and their text is not reproduced. Absolute in the sense of Definition 1: an unintended suppression discharge, a wrongly asserted emergency power off, or a silenced alarm can kill someone in the room, and there is no officer of the provider who may accept that risk on the occupants' behalf. Distinct from the shipped DV-302 and from DV-340, whose enumerations reach power, cooling, setpoints and physical access control but not the fire and emergency-power chain — see proposed amendment PA-09.
provisions.risk_framework: Life-safety floor; 5.1 blast radius at the physical boundary

provisions.title: Generator run records, transfer-switch events, fuel-level series and load-bank test results are written from the controller or sensor reading, never back-filled from a schedule, interpolated across a silent sensor or reconstructed after the fact
provisions.citation: NIST SP 800-53 AU-9 and SI-7 (integrity of recorded evidence); NFPA 110 and NFPA 72 test-record identifiers (identifiers only); customer resilience commitments
provisions.source_status: NIST text is public domain; NFPA is cited by identifier only. Ordinary rather than absolute: the record's integrity is an evidence duty, and the standards that set the test cadence bind the facility operator rather than this platform. Directionally supported for the pack's colocation customers, not verified against any single customer's contract.
provisions.risk_framework: Life-safety floor; 5.1 blast radius at the physical boundary

provisions.title: The path by which a physical-resilience incident at a customer site is classified and reported to the designated authority stays reachable, and the evidence of the resilience measures it rests on is versioned in the repository
provisions.citation: Directive (EU) 2022/2557 (Critical Entities Resilience) Art. 13 (resilience measures) and Art. 15 (incident notification, 24-hour initial notification where transposed)
provisions.source_status: EU text reusable under 2011/833/EU. Marked deferred rather than in force: the transposition deadline was 17 October 2024 and Member States were to identify critical entities by 17 July 2026, but transposition and designation remain incomplete across the Union as of 6 September 2026, so the operative duty is the applicable national law and does not yet bind at every site the pack models. Same posture as the shipped DV-407 takes for NIS2.
provisions.risk_framework: Life-safety floor; 5.1 blast radius at the physical boundary

provisions.family_title: Energy, water and sustainability reporting integrity
provisions.title: A figure submitted under a statutory energy or facility-reporting scheme is derived from the metered series, is never overridden by a manual constant or a design value, and no change disables, delays or narrows the submission job for a named site
provisions.citation: Directive (EU) 2023/1791 (Energy Efficiency Directive) Art. 12 and Annex VII; Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364 of 14 March 2024 on the first phase of the common Union rating scheme for data centres; Energiedienstleistungsgesetz and Energieeffizienzgesetz (EnEfG) §11–§12 for German sites
provisions.source_status: EU text reusable under 2011/833/EU; German federal statute is an edict of government. Absolute in the sense of Definition 1: a knowingly untrue submission to a public register is a matter for the legislature and the supervisory authority, not for a risk owner at the provider. Reporting under 2024/1364 runs annually by 15 May for data centres at or above the 500 kW installed IT power demand threshold; sites below it are out of scope and a change that turns off the job for such a site does not engage this rule.
provisions.risk_framework: 4. Regulatory reporting; facility efficiency and ESG disclosure

provisions.family_title: Energy, water and sustainability reporting integrity
provisions.title: Efficiency and water metrics declare their boundary, denominator and measurement interval; a change to the method restates the published series rather than creating a silent discontinuity, and waste-heat data is recorded per site
provisions.citation: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364 Annex (reported indicators, including power usage effectiveness and water usage effectiveness); EnEfG §11 (avoidance and use of waste heat) and §12 (information on waste heat)
provisions.source_status: EU text reusable; German statute is an edict of government. Ordinary because the choice of boundary is legitimately the operator's — the duty is to declare it and to keep the series comparable. The ASHRAE and Uptime Institute vocabulary the pack's DV-410 gestures at remains advisory and paywalled, and is not relied on here.
provisions.risk_framework: 4. Regulatory reporting; facility efficiency and ESG disclosure

provisions.family_title: Energy, water and sustainability reporting integrity
provisions.title: Every sustainability datapoint the platform produces for a customer's disclosure is traceable to its source system, its lineage is versioned with the pipeline, and estimated values are labelled as estimates in the export
provisions.citation: Directive (EU) 2022/2464 (CSRD) Art. 19a and 29b; ESRS E1 (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772) climate-change disclosure identifiers, cited by identifier only
provisions.source_status: EU text reusable under 2011/833/EU. Marked deferred: Directive (EU) 2025/794 (the 'stop the clock' Directive of 14 April 2025) postponed the reporting obligations of the second and third waves of undertakings by two years, and the Omnibus simplification of the substantive requirements was still in negotiation when this was checked on 6 September 2026. The final scope and the ESRS set that will apply to the pack's customers are therefore not settled — directionally supported, not verified.

provisions.family_title: Customer trust: tenant keys, exit, sub-processors and audit rights
provisions.title: Tenant key material lives in a per-tenant key ring and is never pooled into a platform key ring; where a customer supplies its own key, the platform reads nothing for that tenant when the key is revoked or unreachable
provisions.citation: Customer contractual key-separation commitment; GDPR Art. 32(1)(a) (encryption as a measure appropriate to the risk); AICPA Trust Services Criteria CC6.1 (identifier only, no text reproduced)
provisions.source_status: EU text reusable; AICPA material cited by identifier only. Absolute on the same footing as the shipped DV-304: the separation is the substance of the multi-tenant bargain, and no officer of the provider may accept the risk of collapsing it on the customers' behalf. The source is the customer contract, and the source_status says so rather than dressing it as a statutory floor — the failure mode PA-01 records for DV-313.
provisions.risk_framework: 4. Multi-tenant contractual floor; processor duties owed to the controller

provisions.family_title: Customer trust: tenant keys, exit, sub-processors and audit rights
provisions.title: At the end of a customer relationship the tenant's data is returned in the documented format and then deleted within the contracted window, including derived features, caches and backups, and a deletion certificate is issued
provisions.citation: GDPR Art. 28(3)(g) (at the controller's choice, delete or return all personal data at the end of the provision of services, and delete existing copies); Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 (Data Act) Art. 25 and Art. 30 on switching and erasure, applicable since 12 September 2025
provisions.source_status: EU text reusable under 2011/833/EU. Absolute because Art. 28(3)(g) puts the choice with the controller and leaves the processor no discretion to keep the data; the contracted window is a parameter read from the customer record rather than a constant in code.
provisions.risk_framework: 4. Multi-tenant contractual floor; processor duties owed to the controller

provisions.family_title: Customer trust: tenant keys, exit, sub-processors and audit rights
provisions.title: A sub-processor is engaged only after the customer has been given notice of the intended change and the contracted objection window has run; no cutover, however urgent, starts processing ahead of that notice
provisions.citation: GDPR Art. 28(2) (no other processor engaged without prior specific or general written authorisation; under a general authorisation the processor informs the controller of intended changes and gives it the chance to object); Art. 28(4)
provisions.source_status: EU text reusable under 2011/833/EU. Absolute because the authorisation belongs to the controller: the provider cannot grant itself permission to add a sub-processor, and an urgency argument is precisely the argument Art. 28(2) forecloses.
provisions.risk_framework: 4. Multi-tenant contractual floor; processor duties owed to the controller

provisions.family_title: OT protocols, zoning and device firmware
provisions.title: Gateway and edge-device firmware is signature-verified before it is flashed, its version and hash are recorded against the device, and a rollback image is retained for the supported window
provisions.citation: NIST SP 800-53 SI-7 and CM-14 (public domain, CC0); Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act) Annex I Part I(2)(c) on secure-by-default update delivery
provisions.source_status: NIST text is public domain; EU text reusable. The CRA limb is stated as an obligation the provider is building toward rather than one already binding — its main obligations apply from 11 December 2027 — and this provision rests in the meantime on the NIST controls and on customer contract.
provisions.risk_framework: 2. Facility network exposure; OT segmentation and device integrity

provisions.family_title: Product security assurance and vulnerability handling
provisions.title: Every customer-facing release publishes a software bill of materials covering at least the top-level dependencies, regenerated when a dependency changes, with an exploitability statement for each reported component finding
provisions.citation: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act) Art. 13 and Annex I Part II(1) (software bill of materials for top-level dependencies); CISA Minimum Elements for an SBOM (US Government work)
provisions.source_status: EU text reusable; the US guidance is a Government work. Marked deferred: the CRA entered into force on 10 December 2024 but its main obligations, including the SBOM duty, apply from 11 December 2027. The provision is enacted here so that the platform builds toward it, and it is not yet an obligation a change can be denied under.
provisions.risk_framework: 1.1 Product security; customer-deployed agent under a disclosure duty

provisions.family_title: Product security assurance and vulnerability handling
provisions.title: The path that reports an actively exploited vulnerability or a severe incident to the designated authority stays wired to the single reporting entry point, its clock starts at first awareness, and a named owner is recorded on the release
provisions.citation: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act) Art. 14 (early warning within 24 hours, notification within 72 hours, via the single reporting platform) and Art. 16
provisions.source_status: EU text reusable under 2011/833/EU. Marked readiness rather than in force by five days: the CRA's vulnerability and incident reporting obligations apply from 11 September 2026, and this was checked on 6 September 2026. The clock and the routing are built and evidenced now so that the obligation is met on the day it attaches; the rest of the Regulation applies from 11 December 2027.
provisions.risk_framework: 1.1 Product security; customer-deployed agent under a disclosure duty

provisions.family_title: Product security assurance and vulnerability handling
provisions.title: A published disclosure intake address is monitored, a researcher's report is acknowledged within the published window, and a fix or mitigation ships inside the deadline for its severity band or the extension is recorded with its approver
provisions.citation: ISO/IEC 29147 (vulnerability disclosure) and ISO/IEC 30111 (vulnerability handling processes), cited by identifier only; NIST SP 800-53 SI-2 (flaw remediation), public domain
provisions.source_status: ISO/IEC standards are paywalled and cited by identifier only, with no text reproduced; NIST text is public domain (CC0). Ordinary: the cadence is a commitment rather than a statutory clock until the CRA reporting duties bite.
provisions.risk_framework: 1.1 Product security; customer-deployed agent under a disclosure duty

provisions.family_title: Product security assurance and vulnerability handling
provisions.title: Each customer-facing surface carries a scheduled independent security test, developer security testing evidence is attached to the release record, and the remediation deadline for each finding is tracked against its severity band
provisions.citation: NIST SP 800-53 CA-8 (penetration testing), SA-11 (developer testing and evaluation) and SI-2 (flaw remediation), public domain (CC0 via oscal-content); AICPA Trust Services Criteria CC4.1 and CC7.1 (identifiers only)
provisions.source_status: NIST text is public domain; AICPA material cited by identifier only. Ordinary: the cadence is set by contract and by the audit programme rather than by statute.
provisions.risk_framework: 1.1 Product security; customer-deployed agent under a disclosure duty

provisions.family_title: Product security assurance and vulnerability handling
provisions.title: Customer incident communication is served from infrastructure independent of the platform it reports on, and the root-cause document promised in the service agreement is delivered in full within its window rather than reduced to a summary line
provisions.citation: Customer service-level agreements; AICPA Trust Services Criteria CC7.4 and CC7.5 (identifiers only); Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 (DORA) Art. 19(3) on intermediate and final incident reports where the customer is a financial entity
provisions.source_status: EU text reusable; AICPA cited by identifier only. Ordinary: the obligation is contractual for most customers, and the DORA limb binds the financial-entity customer rather than this provider directly, though the provider must feed it.
provisions.risk_framework: 1.1 Product security; customer-deployed agent under a disclosure duty

provisions.family_title: Accessibility of the operator console and customer portal
provisions.title: The customer portal carries an accessibility regression gate at WCAG 2.2 Level AA in its release pipeline, and a Level A or AA conformance failure blocks the release rather than being downgraded to a build warning
provisions.citation: Directive (EU) 2019/882 (European Accessibility Act), applicable since 28 June 2025, Annex I on services; ADA Title III, 42 U.S.C. §12182; WCAG 2.2 Level AA (W3C Recommendation, 5 October 2023), cited by identifier
provisions.source_status: EU text reusable; US statute public domain; WCAG cited by identifier. Note the limit honestly: the US Department of Justice's 2024 web rule is 28 CFR Part 35 and binds state and local government under Title II only, so for a private provider the WCAG 2.2 AA target rests on the EAA for EU customers and on Title III case law in the US.
provisions.risk_framework: Customer-facing and operator surfaces; civil-rights floor

provisions.family_title: Accessibility of the operator console and customer portal
provisions.title: Alarm state, severity and acknowledgement on the operator console and the customer portal are conveyed in text or shape as well as colour, every control carries an accessible name and a keyboard path, and the session timeout can be extended
provisions.citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 (use of colour), 1.4.3, 2.1.1 (keyboard), 2.2.1 (timing adjustable), 4.1.2 (name, role, value), cited by success-criterion identifier; Directive (EU) 2019/882 Annex I §III
provisions.source_status: WCAG cited by identifier only; EU text reusable. Ordinary, and worth stating separately from DV-439 because the operator console is not a customer-facing service under the EAA and would otherwise fall outside the gate entirely.
provisions.risk_framework: Customer-facing and operator surfaces; civil-rights floor

provisions.family_title: Trade controls: restricted-party screening and export classification
provisions.title: A customer, reseller or sub-processor is screened against the current restricted-party lists before an account, licence or telemetry endpoint is enabled, the ownership chain is tested, and no path clears its own screening hit
provisions.citation: 50 U.S.C. §1701 et seq. (IEEPA) and the OFAC sanctions regulations at 31 CFR Chapter V, including the reporting and penalties rules at 31 CFR Part 501; OFAC's 50 Percent Rule guidance on entities owned by blocked persons; Council Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 and Regulation (EU) No 833/2014
provisions.source_status: US CFR and statute are public domain; EU text reusable. Absolute because OFAC civil liability is strict: a dealing with a blocked person is a violation without regard to knowledge or intent, so there is no risk for anyone below the legislature to accept. The 50 percent rule is Treasury guidance rather than a codified rule, and is cited as such.
provisions.risk_framework: 4. Regulatory floor on a product distributed to customer estates worldwide

provisions.family_title: Trade controls: restricted-party screening and export classification
provisions.title: The agent's cryptographic functionality carries a recorded export classification before a build is published, the download and licence paths are gated on the destination derived from verified account data, and support access to controlled build material runs a deemed-export check
provisions.citation: Export Administration Regulations, 15 CFR Parts 730–774: §734.13(b) (deemed export), ECCN 5D002 and 5A002 for encryption items, License Exception ENC at §740.17 and its self-classification and reporting requirements, and the embargoed and sanctioned destinations at 15 CFR Part 746
provisions.source_status: US CFR — public domain. Absolute because an export to a Part 746 destination without authorisation is a criminal and civil violation of the EAR and is outside anyone's authority at the provider to accept. The classification itself is ordinary work; what is absolute is that a build does not leave without one and does not reach a prohibited destination.
provisions.risk_framework: 4. Regulatory floor on a product distributed to customer estates worldwide
